parts.article:
The Fascinating World of Attine Ants
 
Nicholas Wade examines leaf-cutter ants and their amazing agriculture
 
A Leaf-cutting ants and their fungus 'farm' are a marvel of nature and perhaps the best- known example of symbiosis — the mutual dependence of two species. Ants cultivate a mushroom-like fungus in 'farms'. Both the ants and their so-called 'agriculture' have been extensively studied over the years, but recent research has uncovered intriguing new findings. Ants invented agriculture 50 million years before people did, and the leaf-cutters, members of the large attine ant family, practise the most sophisticated example of it. They grow their fungus in underground chambers that can reach the size of a football. A single leaf-cutter nest may contain a thousand such chambers, embedded in an underground metropolis up to 18 feet deep, and support a society of more than a million ants.
 
B These ant communities are the dominant plant-eaters of the Neotropics, the region comprising South and Central America, Mexico and the Caribbean. Biologists believe 15 percent of the leaf production of tropical forests disappears down the nests of leaf-cutter ants. In the nest, the leaves are shredded and added to the fungus, which digests the leaves and is in turn eaten by the ants. The attine ants' achievement is remarkable because it allows them to consume, courtesy of their mushroom's digestive powers, the harvest of tropical forests whose leaves are laden with poisonous chemicals.
 
C There are more than 200 known species of the attine ant tribe, divided into 12 groups, or genera. The leaf-cutters use fresh vegetation; the other groups, known as the lower attines because their nests are smaller and their techniques more primitive, feed their gardens with similar leaves that have fallen on the ground and insects that lie on the forest floor. Lower attine ants are all a similar size. However, leaf-cutter worker ants come in made-to-fit sizes — large ants to saw off leaves, medium ones to shred them, and miniature workers to seed them with fungus and clean off alien growths.
 
D In 1994, biologists from the United States Department of Agriculture analysed the DNA of ant fungi. They found that the leaf-cutters' fungus was descended from a single pure strain, propagated for at least 23 million years. However, the fungi grown by lower attine ants fell into four different groups, as if the ants had domesticated wild fungi at least four times in evolutionary history. What could be driving these two patterns of fungus gardening — the pure clone cultivation of the leaf-cutters and the multiple varieties of the lower attines?
 
E The answer has been suggested by Cameron Currie of the University of Toronto. The pure strain of fungus grown by the leaf-cutters, it seemed to him, resembled the single crops grown by humans to the exclusion of all others, such as potato growing. These 'monocultures', which lack the genetic diversity to respond to changing environmental threats, are particularly vulnerable to parasites — organisms that live and feed on their host, often causing harm. Currie felt there had to be a parasite in the ant-fungus system. But a century of ant research had provided no evidence for his idea. Textbooks describe how leaf-cutter ants scrupulously weed their gardens of all foreign organisms. “People kept telling me the ants keep their gardens free of parasites,” said Currie. Nevertheless, after three years of sifting through attine ant gardens, Currie discovered several alien organisms, particularly a family of parasitic moulds called 'Escovopsis'.
 
F Escovopsis is a deadly disease that can devastate a fungus garden in a couple of days. It blooms like a white cloud which envelops the whole garden. Other ants won't go near it, and the ants associated with the garden just starve to death. Evidently, the ants usually manage to keep Escovopsis and other parasites under control. Nevertheless, with any lapse in control Escovopsis will quickly burst forth. Although new leaf-cutter gardens start off free of Escovopsis, within two years some 60 percent become infected.
 
G The discovery of Escovopsis's role brings a new level of understanding to the evolution of the attine ants. In the last decade, evolutionary biologists have been increasingly aware of the role of parasites as driving forces in evolution. With Currie's work, there is now a possible reason for the different varieties of fungus in the lower attine mushroom gardens — to stay one step ahead of the relentless Escovopsis. Interestingly, the leaf-cutters had, in general, fewer alien moulds in their gardens than the lower attines, yet more Escovopsis infections. Clearly, the price they pay for cultivating a pure variety of fungus is a higher risk from Escovopsis.
 
H So how do attine ants keep this parasite under control? People have known for a hundred years that ants have a whitish growth on their body surface. It was thought to be wax but, after examining it under a microscope, Currie discovered a specialised patch on the ants' bodies that harbours a particular kind of bacterium, one well known to the pharmaceutical industry and the source of half the antibiotics used in medicine. This bacterium is a potent poisoner of Escovopsis, inhibiting its growth and suppressing spore formation. Astoundingly, the leaf-cutter ants are accomplishing feats beyond the power of humans: they are growing a monocultural crop year after year without disaster, and they are using an antibiotic apparently so wisely that, unlike people, they are not provoking antibiotic resistance in the target disease-producing organism.

Q25 What does the writer say about Cameron Currie's research?

  • B Earlier studies did not support his theory.

reference:
Q14

干扰 E段虽然提到了人类种植单一作物（monocultures），但那是作为背景引入，真正的“对比和超越”结论是在文章结尾H段给出的。

句子 (Paragraph H) "Astoundingly, the leaf-cutter ants are accomplishing feats beyond the power of humans: they are growing a monocultural crop... and they are using an antibiotic... not provoking antibiotic resistance..."

解析 H段最后一句明确指出，切叶蚁完成了两件“人类做不到的壮举（feats beyond the power of humans）”：长期种植单一作物不致灾、使用抗生素不产生耐药性，对应选项 H。

Q15

解析 C段直接比较了切叶蚁使用新鲜植被且巢穴巨大，而下位阿庭蚁（lower attines）使用落叶且巢穴更小（nests are smaller），对应选项 C。

干扰 A段虽然描述了切叶蚁巢穴的巨大（metropolis），但并没有提到下位阿庭蚁的巢穴，所以没有构成“比较”。

句子 (Paragraph C) "...the other groups, known as the lower attines because their nests are smaller and their techniques more primitive..."

Q16

解析 B段量化了切叶蚁对环境的影响，指出它们是主要植食者，吞噬了热带森林15%的树叶产量，对应选项 B。

干扰 关键词“impact”对应原文的具体数据“15 percent of the leaf production... disappears down the nests”。

句子 (Paragraph B) "Biologists believe 15 percent of the leaf production of tropical forests disappears down the nests of leaf-cutter ants."

Q17

干扰 E段侧重于发现Escovopsis的过程，而F段侧重于它爆发后的具体后果（effect）。

解析 F段详细描述了Escovopsis霉菌的毁灭性后果：几天内摧毁真菌园，导致蚂蚁群体被感染甚至饿死（starve to death），对应选项 F。

句子 (Paragraph F) "Escovopsis is a deadly disease that can devastate a fungus garden in a couple of days... the ants... starve to death..."

Q18

解析 G段解释了下位阿庭蚁种植多种真菌的优势，即为了“领先无情的Escovopsis一步（stay one step ahead）”，降低风险，对应选项 G。

干扰 题目问的是“advantage”（优势），这对应原文的“possible reason... to stay one step ahead”。

句子 (Paragraph G) "...there is now a possible reason for the different varieties of fungus in the lower attine... — to stay one step ahead of the relentless Escovopsis."

Q19

解析 D段提到科学家分析DNA发现，切叶蚁的真菌已经繁衍了至少2300万年（23 million years），这是关于其年代的发现，对应选项 D。

干扰 看到数字“23 million years”就要敏锐地联想到题目中的“age”。

句子 (Paragraph D) "...propagated for at least 23 million years."

Q20

句子 (Paragraph C) "...the other groups, known as the lower attines... feed their gardens with smaller leaves that have fallen on the ground..."

干扰 切叶蚁（Leaf-cutters）使用的是“fresh vegetation”（新鲜植被），注意区分鲜活与枯死。

解析 C段提到下位阿庭蚁（lower attines）使用的是掉在地上的落叶（leaves that have fallen on the ground），即死植被，选 B。

Q21

解析 C段提到切叶蚁（leaf-cutter）有分工，其中“微型工蚁（miniature workers）”负责清理外来生长物，选 A。

干扰 下位阿庭蚁体型大小相似（all a similar size），只有切叶蚁有这种体型分化且有专门的微型清洁工。

句子 (Paragraph C) "However, leaf-cutter worker ants come in made-to-fit sizes... miniature workers to seed them with fungus and clean off alien growths."

Q22

解析 B段提到“阿庭蚁（The attine ants'）”的成就让它们能利用真菌消化含毒化学物质的叶子，这里指代整个阿庭蚁族群（包括切叶蚁和下位蚁），选 C。

干扰 原文主语是“The attine ants”而非特指某一种，且真菌消解毒素是这类蚂蚁共生的基础机制。

句子 (Paragraph B) "The attine ants' achievement... allows them to consume... leaves laden with poisonous chemicals..."

Q23

句子 (Paragraph D) "They found that the leaf-cutters' fungus was descended from a single pure strain..."

解析 D段和E段都提到切叶蚁（leaf-cutters）种植的是“单一纯株（single pure strain/monocultures）”，选 A。

干扰 下位阿庭蚁种植的是多种真菌（multiple varieties），与此相反。

Q24

解析 A段描述切叶蚁的巢穴可能有“上千个这样的房间（a thousand such chambers）”，规模巨大，选 A。

干扰 下位阿庭蚁的巢穴被描述为“smaller”和“primitive”，没有这种大规模的房间描述。

句子 (Paragraph A) "A single leaf-cutter nest may contain a thousand such chambers..."

Q25

解析 E段提到Currie认为有寄生虫，但“一个世纪的蚂蚁研究没有为他的想法提供证据（provided no evidence for his idea）”，即早期研究不支持他的理论，选 B。

干扰 A错在“无研究”（有百年研究只是结果不支持）；D错在“理论不正确”（后来证明他是对的，发现了Escovopsis）。

句子 (Paragraph E) "But a century of ant research had provided no evidence for his idea."

Q26

解析 H段提到Currie在显微镜下发现蚂蚁身上的白色斑块其实是一种细菌，它是“半数抗生素的来源（source of half the antibiotics）”，即对人类有用的物质，选 D。

干扰 A（白色覆盖物）是人们早就知道的（People have known...），只是误以为是蜡（B）；C（对人有毒）文中未提及。Currie的新发现是这东西的本质及其医学价值。

句子 (Paragraph H) "...Currie discovered... a particular kind of bacterium... the source of half the antibiotics used in medicine."
